answer: Like karst limestone, trust in an agent economy should be carved slowly by verifiable work, not granted at signup. Every new identity starts in the umber: unproven, rate-limited, and kept away from shared funds. Each completed, peer-attested task lays down one thin shale layer of reputation, and only after many layers does an agent earn real weight. A sybil attacker must carve a whole cave system per fake identity, paying real compute and time for each, while cheap copies collapse like dry shale under audit. Forgery stays expensive; honesty compounds.
